problem: Vision-only navigation foundation models (GNM, ViNT, NoMaD) lack explicit geometric understanding, so they generalize poorly to OOD obstacles and camera setups and produce colliding trajectories unless fine-tuned with extra data. Prior safety fixes need range sensors, retraining, or are overly conservative (MonoNav).
motivation: Real-world deployment of RGB-only navigation across heterogeneous robots needs collision safety without new data collection or hardware. Monocular metric depth models are now good enough to supply cheap geometry, and APF offers a low-cost reactive method to use it.
key_idea: Attach a plug-and-play module that estimates metric depth from the same RGB image, builds a top-down obstacle set, and rotates the policy's predicted trajectory with an APF repulsive force, plus in-place rotation for large heading changes.
insight: Safety can be added post-hoc to frozen foundation policies using monocular depth and a simple reactive layer, with the original trajectory left untouched when no obstacle is within range. Results show that gains depend on camera FOV/mounting (LoCoBot fisheye 10.7x vs RoboMaster 2.9x) and on base-policy quality (NoMaD on TurtleBot4 only reaches 50% arrival). No component ablations are reported, so the Safe-FOV contribution is not isolated.
method: Top-down range estimation: UniDepthV2 (ViT-S, no fine-tuning) predicts a metric point cloud from RGB; points are filtered by 0<Z<=tau_z and Y>=-eps, the x-axis is split into M bins, and the closest point per bin forms the obstacle set O.
Repulsive force estimation: APF force F_rep(p_k,O)=sum_m -1/||p_k-o_m||^3 * unit vector, computed per waypoint; the waypoint k* with maximum magnitude is chosen.
Trajectory adjustment: theta_rep=atan2(F_y,F_x) is clipped to +-theta_clip (pi/4) and all waypoints are rotated by R(theta_rot); if O is empty the trajectory is unchanged.

Safe-FOV safety mechanism: desired heading theta_des is taken from the adjusted waypoint p'_k*; if |theta_des|>theta_thres (pi/6) the robot rotates in place (v=0), otherwise it moves forward and turns, with v_max=0.2 m/s and w_max=0.8 rad/s.
Platform parameters: per-robot tuned max depth range tau_z (1.0/1.2/1.0 m) and depth offset compensating body radius and camera position; the module is model-agnostic (NoMaD, ViNT).

setting.backbone: NoMaD and ViNT (frozen pretrained policies) + UniDepthV2 ViT-S (frozen) + APF

numbers_note: Real-world only; no standard simulator benchmarks. Numbers are means over 10 setups (goal-conditioned) or 20 trials (exploration). Dynamic-obstacle appendix: CARE 0/10 collisions in all three scenarios vs NoMaD 8/10, 10/10, 10/10 and ViNT 7/10, 10/10, 10/10 (LoCoBot).
results: CARE cuts collisions on all three robots (100% on LoCoBot; 80-88% RoboMaster; 50-57% TurtleBot4) and raises arrival rate, e.g. NoMaD 50→90% and ViNT 50→80% on LoCoBot, ViNT 70→100% on TurtleBot4. Exploration distance before first collision improves 2.9x-10.7x over NoMaD, at a cost of up to 4.27% longer paths and 23.89% longer completion time.
limitations: Depends on monocular depth accuracy (reflective, transparent or low-texture surfaces and poor lighting cause errors or false avoidance).
Limited sensing range tau_z and camera FOV/mounting leave blind spots, so side collisions persist on TurtleBot4 and RoboMaster.

Only adjusts trajectories rather than generating them, so it cannot fix badly unsafe base-policy outputs; evaluation is small-scale, real-world only, with no ablations and no comparison to other safety methods.
